open-question.question: Where should the maintainer instructions for the build script live: a --help/usage block in the script, a "Build from source / Release" section in docs/macOS.md like docs/Linux.md has, a separate maintainer doc, or a combination?
open-question.alternative: The script gets a `--help`/usage block listing its flags and prerequisites, and `docs/macOS.md` ends with an "(Alternative): Build from Source / Release" section, matching `docs/Linux.md`. That section walks through clone, installing the toolchain (including `cargo install mopro-cli`, which is not on this machine yet), running the script, and publishing the dmg and its SHA-256. It follows the precedent already set by `docs/Linux.md` (download → verify → run → "Build from Source"). A maintainer at the terminal and a reader browsing `docs/` each find instructions where they look, and it needs no new file beyond the user guide the milestone already requires. The same instructions live in two places: the script's usage text and the doc section. They can drift apart whenever flags or prerequisites change. The section also mixes maintainer release steps (publishing the checksum, and tagging too if the tag becomes a requirement) into a guide meant for end users, who mostly only need to download, check the checksum and get past Gatekeeper.

All maintainer guidance lives in the script itself, in a header comment plus a `--help`/usage block covering prerequisites, flags, outputs and the release checklist. `docs/macOS.md` stays a pure end-user guide, with at most a one-line pointer to the script. There is one source of truth, and it sits next to the code it describes, so it is the easiest to keep accurate as the script changes. The user guide stays short and focused on download, checksum, install and Gatekeeper. It breaks the pattern of `docs/Linux.md`, which gives readers a "Build from Source" path in the docs. Anyone browsing `docs/` or GitHub can't find how releases are made unless they already know the script exists. Steps that happen outside the script, such as attaching the dmg and its checksum to the GitHub release, fit awkwardly in usage text.

The full maintainer instructions go in a "Build from Source / Release" section of `docs/macOS.md`, as in `docs/Linux.md`. The script prints only a minimal usage line, or an error that points to the doc, and has no detailed help of its own. It is the closest match to the existing Linux guide, keeps all prose documentation in the `docs/` tree where the platform guides already live, and keeps the script lean with nothing to duplicate. A maintainer running the script has no built-in reference for its flags or prerequisites and has to switch to the doc. The user-facing guide also carries release-maintainer content. This matters more if the script ends up with several flags, for example for `mopro build` handling or a clean build.

A dedicated maintainer document is added alongside a `--help` block in the script. It could be a `docs/macOS-release.md`, a general `RELEASING.md`, or a README next to the script. `docs/macOS.md` stays user-facing and links to the maintainer doc, if it mentions building at all. It cleanly separates the two audiences. End users get a short, focused guide, and maintainers get room for the full release procedure: toolchain setup, the version-consistency warning, verification output, and publishing the dmg and checksum. A general `RELEASING.md` could also later cover Linux and Windows, which have no build scripts today. It adds another file for a small repo that has no maintainer-doc convention yet. It also still duplicates part of the script's usage text. How natural a README next to the script is depends on where the script ends up living, which is a separate open question.
open-question.recommendation: It follows the docs/Linux.md precedent the goal asks for, gives maintainers help at the terminal and a browsable release section in the guide, and with a script that has almost no flags the duplication between the two stays small.
